title: Perpendicular distance to a plane
section: Chapter 3 Review Questions ▷ Distance to a Plane
terms: point-to-plane distance; orthogonal foot; distance between parallel planes.

exposition.text:
For a plane n · x = d with n ̸= 0, the distance from P is |n · P − d|/∥n∥. The signed numerator
measures normal displacement in the scale set by n, and dividing by its norm converts it to
2
Euclidean length. The orthogonal foot is Q = P − [(n · P − d)/∥n∥ ]n.
For parallel planes written with the same normal, the separation is |d − d |/∥n∥. If the normals
1 2
are proportional but unequal, rescale the equations first. Squared distance to a plane is often
convenient in optimization and avoids absolute values.
Reflection across a plane sends P to 2Q − P , where Q is its orthogonal foot. Equating distances
to two planes generally produces two angle-bisector planes. For a sphere of radius R whose
center is distance d from a plane, the minimum and maximum point-to-plane distances are
max{d − R, 0} and d + R.

question.text:
What is the distance between 2x − y + 2z = 3 and 4x − 2y + 4z = 18?
(A) 1 (B) 2 (C) 3 (D) 4 (E) 5

solution.text:
Divide the second equation by 2 to obtain the same normal: 2x − y + 2z = 9. The separation

question.text:
On the sphere centered at (1, 1, 1) with radius 3, what are the minimum and maximum dis-
tances to the plane x + 2y + 2z = 11?
(A) 1, 5 (B) 0, 5 (C) 0, 3 (D) 1, 3 (E) 2, 5

solution.text:
The center is at distance |5 − 11|/3 = 2 from the plane. Signed normal displacements from
points of the sphere range from −2 − 3 = −5 to −2 + 3 = 1. Since this interval includes zero,
the sphere meets the plane and the minimum distance is zero; the maximum is five. Taking
|2 − 3| as the minimum would miss the intersection.
